evidence.effect_or_condition: U.S. indications and major labeled safety warnings
evidence.population: U.S. prescribing population as specified by indication
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 U.S. DailyMed label for escitalopram tablets identifies escitalopram as an SSRI indicated for major depressive disorder in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older and for generalized anxiety disorder in adults and pediatric patients 7 years and older, and carries a boxed warning regarding suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients.
evidence.safety_note: Label language is product-, jurisdiction-, and revision-specific; the cited prescribing information also includes serotonin syndrome, discontinuation, bleeding, hyponatremia, seizure, and mania or hypomania precautions.

evidence.dose_or_duration: 522 randomized controlled trials across 21 antidepressants; acute treatment
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2018 network meta-analysis of 522 randomized trials involving 116,477 adults found all 21 included antidepressants more efficacious than placebo for acute major depressive disorder; escitalopram was among the included treatments, with comparative efficacy and acceptability varying across head-to-head comparisons and evidence certainty ranging from moderate to very low.
evidence.safety_note: Network-level estimates describe average short-term treatment effects and do not determine the best medication for an individual.

evidence.study_type: pooled analysis of three randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials
evidence.population: adults aged 18 to 80 years with generalized anxiety disorder
evidence.supported_claim_language: A pooled analysis of three similarly designed eight-week randomized placebo-controlled trials involving approximately 850 adults with generalized anxiety disorder found greater improvement in Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale scores with escitalopram than placebo.
evidence.safety_note: The evidence is short term and trial eligibility limits generalization to patients with substantial comorbidity or populations not represented in the studies.

evidence.effect_or_condition: treatment-emergent sexual dysfunction during major depressive disorder treatment
evidence.study_type: two randomized double-blind placebo-controlled comparative trials
evidence.population: adults with major depressive disorder and normal sexual functioning at baseline
evidence.supported_claim_language: Two randomized double-blind placebo-controlled studies comparing escitalopram with bupropion XL found treatment-emergent sexual dysfunction was more frequent with escitalopram than with bupropion XL or placebo among participants with normal sexual functioning at baseline.
evidence.safety_note: These older short-term trials address selected sexual-function outcomes in adults with major depressive disorder and do not establish overall comparative superiority or individualized medication choice.

evidence.effect_or_condition: U.S. indications and major labeled safety warnings
evidence.population: U.S. prescribing population as specified by indication
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 U.S. DailyMed label for bupropion hydrochloride extended-release tablets (XL) identifies the product as an aminoketone antidepressant indicated for major depressive disorder and prevention of seasonal major depressive episodes in seasonal affective disorder, and carries a boxed warning regarding suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients.
evidence.safety_note: This source is specific to the extended-release XL product and includes dose-related seizure risk and hypertension warnings; evidence for smoking cessation or other formulations must remain indication- and product-specific.

evidence.dose_or_duration: 522 randomized controlled trials across 21 antidepressants; acute treatment
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2018 network meta-analysis of 522 randomized trials involving 116,477 adults found all 21 included antidepressants more efficacious than placebo for acute major depressive disorder; bupropion was among the included treatments, with comparative efficacy and acceptability varying across head-to-head comparisons and evidence certainty ranging from moderate to very low.
evidence.safety_note: Network-level estimates describe average short-term treatment effects and do not determine the best medication for an individual.

evidence.population: adults with major depressive disorder represented across included studies
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2016 systematic review and meta-analysis of 51 studies found placebo-controlled evidence supporting bupropion's antidepressant efficacy, while many head-to-head comparisons found broadly similar depression outcomes to other antidepressants and study heterogeneity limited strong comparative conclusions.
evidence.safety_note: The review combines studies with different formulations, designs, comparators, and populations; it does not establish an individualized treatment choice.

evidence.effect_or_condition: treatment-emergent sexual dysfunction during major depressive disorder treatment
evidence.study_type: two randomized double-blind placebo-controlled comparative trials
evidence.population: adults with major depressive disorder and normal sexual functioning at baseline
evidence.supported_claim_language: Two randomized double-blind placebo-controlled studies comparing bupropion XL with escitalopram found treatment-emergent sexual dysfunction was less frequent with bupropion XL than with escitalopram among participants with normal sexual functioning at baseline.
evidence.safety_note: These older short-term trials are formulation- and outcome-specific; lower rates of selected sexual adverse effects do not establish overall comparative superiority or individualized medication choice.
